Slice 10 of [Release 2: implementation](https://github.com/chrisdoc/surveybeat-next/issues/101).

## Goal
German Teams get German Questions, and redaction handles German contact details.

## Acceptance criteria
- The weekly team health Template carries its Questions, labels, and options in English and German; a new Pulse copies them in the Lead's language; existing Pulses are unchanged.
- Redaction (ADR 0009) recognises German phone formats (+49, 0 prefixes, spaces, slashes, dashes) with table tests.

## Tests
- Domain tests for the Template copy and redaction cases.

## Follows
ADR 0018, ADR 0009

## Context

Planned on the [Wayfinder map](https://github.com/chrisdoc/surveybeat-next/issues/85). Use `GLOSSARY.md` terms throughout. ADRs are in `docs/adr/`; research in `docs/research/`.

00cfa26d ADR 0019: AI-written discussion guide, Lead only; glossary Discussion guide (#100)
# German ships as typed catalogs per locale, a prerendered answer page per locale, and a bilingual Template

Release 2 adds German to the app, the answer page, and emails ([research](../research/german-localization.md)).

- **Catalogs:** each catalog gets a `de.ts` beside the English one, typed so a missing key, an extra key, or a wrong `{placeholder}` fails typecheck. The message functions take the locale instead of the fixed `"en"`; plurals, dates, and numbers come from `Intl` for that locale.
- **Which language:** a Person's own setting, then the browser's languages, then the Organization's default. Emails render in the language stored with the send when it is created.
- **Answer page:** one prerendered page per locale (`/a`, `/de/a`), each loading only its own answer catalog. The Invitation link picks the page from the recipient's language. ADR 0008's budget applies to each page separately.
- **Words:** informal "du". Pulse and Team stay English; Round → Runde, Lead → Teamleitung, Organization → Organisation, Submission → Einsendung. Claude drafts, the product owner reviews in the PR.
- **Template:** the weekly team health Template ships in both languages; a new Pulse copies its Questions in the Lead's language. Existing Pulses keep their Questions.
- **Privacy:** the language is never stored with a Submission or an Answer. In a small Team it could single out the one German reader.

## Consequences

- The budget test runs per answer page.
- Pages rendered in `MainWorker.ts` (delivery time, unsubscribe) hold hard-coded English and must move to the catalog.
- Redaction gains German phone number cases.
- A Team with mixed languages sees the Pulse's Questions in the language they were created in.

1. Add `GERMAN_PHONE_PATTERN`, applied as a new step BEFORE the generic phone step (after handles). Shape:

   - boundaries: not preceded by a word char, "+" or digit; not followed by a word char, and not followed by `[.,]\d` (so it never cuts into a larger number/date).

<result>Findings from probing `Redaction.ts` with about 90 inputs (all outputs below are real). I ran no ReDoS-style input over 2.5 ms and did not run the existing test suite.

**MAJOR: date guard leaks a phone number that follows a date or year range (fail-open privacy gap).**
- `"12.11.2026 12345678"` → unchanged
- `"Am 12.11.2026 12 34 56 78"` → unchanged
- `"12.34.5678 9"` → unchanged
- Cause: `DATE_OR_YEAR_RANGE_PATTERNS` only tests the start of `p1`, and the generic `PHONE_PATTERN` match can run past the date. When the guard hits, the whole match is returned, including the trailing digits. "Termin 12.11.2026 0171 ..." is fine because the German step runs first. A non-German or separator-less tail after a date is not.
- Fix: when the guard hits, strip only the date prefix, then re-evaluate the remainder (at least 7 digits plus a separator) and redact that. Alternatively, tighten the guard to match the whole `p1`. The year-range pattern already uses `$`, so the other three are inconsistent with it.

**MINOR: generic step still redacts the first digit group after a date or range as "phone", with the partial-match fallout.**
- `"1.2.2024 5551234 99"` → `"1.2.[phone]"`. The date is mangled because `1.2.2024 5551234 99` was not guarded, since the date pattern needs a 4-digit year and `1.2.2024` does match it. So here the guard didn't fire because the match started at a different offset. This is odd partial-match behaviour.
- `"2020 - 2024 555 1234"` → `"2020 - [phone]"`. The range guard has `$`, so it never fires when anything follows.

**MINOR: false positives (over-match), all from the generic step and likely pre-existing, but the issue says plain numbers must not match.**
- `"10 000 000 Euro"` → `"[phone] Euro"`
- `"Jahr 2019 2020 2021"` → `"Jahr [phone]"`
- `"2019 2020 2021 2022"` → `"[phone]"`
- `"Nr. 12 345 678"` → `"Nr. [phone]"`
- `"Bestellung 0123 4567"` → `"Bestellung [phone]"`
- `"ID 0815 4711"` → `"ID [phone]"`
- `"Budget 0 100 200 300"` → `"Budget 0 [phone]"`
- `"DE89 3704 0044 0532 0130 00"` → `"DE89 [phone] [phone]"`. An IBAN being redacted is arguably desirable.
- I did not compare against `main`, so I can't say which of these predate the diff. The German step's digit-count window (7–12) also treats "0123 4567" and "0815 4711" as phones. That is probably acceptable given the privacy bias, but you should decide on purpose.

**MINOR: leading-"0" separated groups leave a stray "0".**
- `"0 30 12 34 56"` → `"0 [phone]"`
- `"0 170 1234567"` → `"0 [phone]"`
- The number is redacted except for the leading 0. This is harmless, but a table test should pin it down or the pattern should allow `0 ` as a prefix.

**Not a problem (checked):**
- All of these redact correctly:
  - `+49 (0)170 1234567`
  - `0049(0)30 1234567`
  - `Tel.: 030 1234567-0`
  - `+49 30 123 456-78`
  - `(030) 1234567`
  - `0170/1234567`
  - `0171 / 123 45 67.`
  - `+49-170-1234567`
  - `01701234567`
  - `03012345678`
  - `030 1234567.` and `030 1234567,`
  - numbers in parentheses
  - `tel 030.1234567`
- Not over-matched: `1.250,00`, `Kosten 0,50`, `14:30 bis 16:45`, `Q3/2026`, `Sprint 23-24`, `10-15 Leute`, `Raum 0.12`, `v2.0.1`, `Version 2.0.1.3`, `2020-2024`, `01.02.2024`, `1.2.2024`, `10.11.26`, `2024/11/10`, `15.10. 20.11. 30.12.`, `1234567` and `0123456`.
- A real number after a date is caught when the German pattern applies: `12.11.2026 030 1234567` → `12.11.2026 [phone]`, and `2026-11-10 0170 1234567` → `2026-11-10 [phone]`.
- ReDoS: adversarial 960–990-char strings took at most 2.5 ms, with repeated `1 `, `3/`, `1.` and long zero runs. There is no risk.

**Unchanged and arguably expected:**
- `"Tel 5551234567"` (10 plain digits, no separators) is not redacted. That is the existing "keep plain numbers" rule.

Probe scripts are at `/tmp/claude-1001/-home-ubuntu--t3-worktrees-surveybeat-next-t3-4489afcd-9256957e8ff1b83e/930bf514-4be3-4546-8b66-4019a45d831f/scratchpad/p.ts` and `q.ts`. Code is in `/home/ubuntu/.t3/worktrees/surveybeat-next/t3-4489afcd-9256957e8ff1b83e/packages/domain/src/privacy/Redaction.ts`.

Verdict: no BLOCKER. One MAJOR to fix: the date guard returns the entire match when the match starts with a date, so a following phone number leaks.</result>
